questions.question:
Fill in the blank with most appropriate option:
That was the ___ performance of the night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**most amazing**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The blank in the sentence is asking for a superlative adjective to describe the performance.
 
• The word "**most amazing**" is the correct superlative form of the adjective "**amazing**."
 
• Superlative adjectives are used to describe the highest degree of a quality among three or more entities.
 
• **Options 1, 2,** and **4** are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1: "amazing"** is a positive adjective, not a superlative.
 
• **Option 2: "more amazing"** is a comparative adjective, not a superlative.
 
• **Option 4: "much amazing"** is grammatically incorrect.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"That was the **most amazing**__ performance of the night."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Positive Adjective:** "Amazing" is the base form of the adjective.
 
• **Comparative Adjective:** "More amazing" is used to compare two entities.
 
• **Superlative Adjective:** "Most amazing" is used to describe the highest degree of quality among three or more entities.
</ul

questions.question: The phrase "The stars danced in the sky" is an example of ___.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**2**' i.e. personification.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• Personification is a literary device where human qualities or abilities are attributed to non-human entities or objects.
 
• In the given phrase, "The stars danced in the sky," the stars are described as performing a human action, "danced," which is an example of personification.
 
• Options 1 (metaphor), 3 (simile), and 4 (idiom) are incorrect because they do not involve assigning human characteristics to non-human things.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The phrase "The stars danced in the sky" is an example of **personification**__."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Metaphor** is incorrect because metaphors compare two things without using "like" or "as," but they do not involve assigning human traits.
 
• **Option 3: Simile** is incorrect because similes compare two things using "like" or "as," which is not the case in the given phrase.
 
• **Option 4: Idiom** is incorrect because idioms are phrases with figurative meanings different from their literal meanings, which does not apply here.
</ul

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

She sang (1) / so beautifully (2) / that everyone (3) / were amazed(4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is located in **part (4)** of the sentence due to a **subject-verb agreement** mistake.
 
• The word "**everyone**" is an indefinite pronoun. In English grammar, indefinite pronouns like *everyone, everybody, someone,* and *nobody* are always treated as **singular subjects**.
 
• Since the subject is singular, it must be followed by the singular verb "**was**" instead of the plural verb "**were**."
 
• Therefore, the phrase "were amazed" must be corrected to "**was amazed**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She sang so beautifully that **everyone was amazed**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "She sang"** – This part is correct; "sang" is the simple past tense of the verb "sing."
 
• **2: "so beautifully"** – The adverb "beautifully" correctly modifies the verb "sang." The word "so" is used here as an adverb of degree.
 
• **3: "that everyone"** – This correctly introduces a result clause using the "**so... that**" construction, which is used to express cause and effect.
 
• **Singular Indefinite Pronouns:** Other words that always take a singular verb include: *each, either, neither, anyone, anybody, anything, someone, somebody, something, no one, nobody,* and *nothing*.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

He drives very careful (1) / especially at night (2) / to avoid any accidents (3) / on the road(4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is found in **part (1)** of the sentence due to the incorrect use of an adjective instead of an adverb.
 
• The word "**careful**" is an adjective, which is used to describe a noun (e.g., "He is a *careful* driver").
 
• However, in this sentence, the word is modifying the verb "**drives**." To modify a verb, an **adverb** must be used.
 
• The adverbial form of "careful" is "**carefully**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He drives **very carefully** especially at night to avoid any accidents on the road."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **2: "especially at night"** – This part is correct. "Especially" is used to single out a particular time or circumstance.
 
• **3: "to avoid any accidents"** – This part uses the "to-infinitive" correctly to express the purpose or reason for the action.
 
• **4: "on the road"** – This is the correct prepositional phrase indicating the location.
 
• **Grammar Rule:** Most adverbs are formed by adding **-ly** to the adjective (e.g., *quick → quickly, happy → happily*). Always check if you are describing an **action** (use an adverb) or a **thing/person** (use an adjective).

questions.question:

(2) The students greeted her.
(3) She smiled at them and replied.
(4) The lesson began.

The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sequence follows the logical progression of events in the classroom.
 
• **Sentence 1:** "The teacher entered the class" introduces the main character and sets the scene.
 
• **Sentence 2:** "The students greeted her" logically follows as a response to the teacher’s entry.
 
• **Sentence 3:** "She smiled at them and replied" is a natural continuation of the interaction between the teacher and students.
 
• **Sentence 4:** "The lesson began" concludes the sequence with the teacher starting the lesson after the initial interaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Logical arrangement of sentences is crucial to maintain coherence and clarity in a paragraph.
 
• When arranging sentences, start with the sentence that introduces the setting or main character, followed by actions or responses in chronological order.

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:**

"The teacher entered the class. The students greeted her. She smiled at them and replied. The lesson began."

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

I bought an apple (1) / a banana (2) / and a orange (3) / from the market(4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in **part (3)** of the sentence because of the incorrect use of the indefinite article "**a**."
 
• In English, the article "**an**" must be used before words that begin with a **vowel sound** (a, e, i, o, u).
 
• The word "**orange**" begins with the vowel sound **/ɔː/**, which requires the article "**an**" instead of "a."
 
• The article "a" is reserved for words beginning with a consonant sound (e.g., *a banana, a market*).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I bought an apple, a banana **and an orange** from the market."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "I bought an apple"** – This is correct as "apple" starts with a vowel sound.
 
• **2: "a banana"** – This is correct as "banana" starts with a consonant sound.
 
• **4: "from the market"** – This is a correct prepositional phrase indicating the source of the purchase.
 
• **Sound vs. Letter Rule:** Always focus on the **initial sound** rather than the letter. For example, we say "**an** hour" (silent 'h') but "**a** university" (starts with a 'y' consonant sound).

• In English grammar, a noun (like "**decision**") must be modified by an **adjective**.
 
• The word "**quickly**" is an adverb, which is typically used to modify verbs (e.g., "He ran *quickly*").
 
• To correct the sentence, the adverb "quickly" should be replaced with the adjective "**quick**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He made a **quick decision** without considering all the facts."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "He made a"** – This part is correct. "Make a decision" is a common colocation, and "made" is the correct past tense form.
 
• **3: "without considering"** – This part is correct. The preposition "without" is followed by the **gerund** form of the verb ("considering").
 
• **4: "all the facts"** – This is a grammatically correct noun phrase acting as the object of the gerund.
 
• **Grammar Rule:** Remember that **Adjectives** describe "what kind" of noun (a *quick* decision, a *loud* noise), while **Adverbs** describe "how" an action is performed (decided *quickly*, shouted *loudly*).

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

She returned back (1) / the borrowed books (2) / to the library (3) / on time (4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in **part (1)** of the sentence because of **redundancy** (pleonasm).
 
• The verb "**return**" itself means "to give back," "to send back," or "to come back."
 
• Adding the word "**back**" after "returned" is unnecessary and repetitive, as the meaning of "back" is already included in the verb.
 
• To correct this, you should either say "**She returned the borrowed books**" or "**She gave back the borrowed books**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She **returned the borrowed books** to the library on time."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **2: "the borrowed books"** – This part is correct. "Borrowed" is a past participle used as an adjective to describe the books.
 
• **3: "to the library"** – This is the correct prepositional phrase indicating the destination of the return.
 
• **4: "on time"** – This is a correct idiomatic expression meaning "at the planned or expected time."
 
• **Common Redundancies to Avoid:** Similar errors include: 
 
 
• *Revert back* (Use "Revert")
 
• *Reply back* (Use "Reply")
 
• *Repeat again* (Use "Repeat")
 
• *New innovation* (Use "Innovation")
